creatures.name: Bulleto
creatures.education: The bullet ant has the most painful insect sting in the world! People say being stung feels like getting hit by a bullet, and the pain lasts for 24 hours. Indigenous tribes in the Amazon have a famous bravery ceremony where young warriors wear gloves filled with these ants without crying!
creatures.exploration_trait: Pincer Clamp (Can snip tough jungle wire-vines and grip onto swaying canopy ropes).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy reddish-black armor plates, huge golden-fringed mandibles, and an intimidating curved abdominal stinger.

creatures.name: Foliacutter
creatures.education: Leafcutter ants don't actually eat the leaves they carry! They are nature's first farmers. They take the cut leaf umbrellas into underground cathedrals, chew them into mulch, and use it to grow a special white mushroom fungus that feeds the whole million-ant colony!
creatures.exploration_trait: Leaf Parasol (Carries wide jungle leaves to shield the player from tropical acid rain and burning sun).
creatures.visual_notes: Rust-brown body with sharp spiky thoracic thorns, carrying a glowing crescent-cut jungle leaf overhead.

creatures.name: Morphina
creatures.education: The blue morpho's wings aren't actually blue at all! They have no blue pigment. Instead, their wings are covered in microscopic diamond-shaped scales that bend and reflect sunlight, causing brilliant iridescent blue light to flash as they flutter through the dark jungle.
creatures.exploration_trait: Flash Dazzle (Blinds cave predators with a flash of iridescent blue light, canceling hostile agro).
creatures.visual_notes: Breathtaking metallic cobalt-blue wings rimmed in midnight black, with owl-eye spots on the brown underside.

creatures.name: Titanus
creatures.education: The titan beetle can grow up to 6.5 inches long—longer than an adult human hand! Its curved mandibles are so strong they can snap wooden pencils clean in half and can even tear through thick leather work gloves.
creatures.exploration_trait: Wood-Bore Saw (Saws through fallen hardwood logs that block ancient forest pathways).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive reddish-brown leathery elytra, long sweeping serrated antennae, and formidable curved jaws.

creatures.name: Peanuthead
creatures.habitat: Trunks of Massive Ceiba & Rubber Trees
creatures.education: This bizarre bug has a giant hollow head that looks like an unshelled peanut or a sleeping alligator snout! If a monkey tries to eat it, it pops open its back wings to reveal two giant fake owl eyes to terrify the attacker.
creatures.exploration_trait: Fake-Eye Lantern (Illuminates dark forest clearings and scares away timid woodland critters).
creatures.visual_notes: Bulbous textured peanut-shaped snout, speckled bark-camouflage wings, and large yellow-and-black eye spots.

creatures.name: Birdeater
creatures.education: The Goliath birdeater is the largest spider on Earth by mass—as big as a dinner plate and weighing as much as a puppy! Despite their name, they rarely eat birds. When scared, they rub their hairy legs together to make a loud hissing rattle heard 15 feet away!
creatures.exploration_trait: Burrow Tap (Taps the ground to reveal hidden hollow roots and secret subterranean trapdoors).
creatures.visual_notes: Enormous velvety chestnut-brown spider with thick hairy limbs, large curved fangs, and gold knee hairs.

creatures.name: Whiplash
creatures.habitat: Dark Caves, Hollow Trees & Rock Crevices
creatures.education: Whip spiders look terrifying, but they are completely harmless to humans with zero venom! Their front two legs have evolved into ultra-long whip antennas that can feel obstacles and smell prey in complete, pitch-black darkness.
creatures.exploration_trait: Whip Radar (Detects hidden cavern walls, unseen traps, and invisible ledges in total darkness).
creatures.visual_notes: Flat crab-like body with spiky raptorial pedipalps and two whip-like feelers three times its body length.

creatures.name: Trapjaw
creatures.education: The trap-jaw ant has one of the fastest predatory movements in the entire animal kingdom! It locks its jaws open at 180 degrees and snaps them shut at 140 miles per hour! If an ant needs to escape a predator, it snaps its jaws against the ground to catapult itself backward through the air!
creatures.exploration_trait: Recoil Jump (Snaps mandibles against stone to vault itself onto high ledges to retrieve items).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender amber body with giant straight jaws locked wide open like a cocked bear trap.

creatures.name: Army-March
creatures.education: Army ants never build permanent nests! Instead, the entire colony of 700,000 ants links their claws together to form a living ball of ants called a 'bivouac' that protects the queen and larvae. When they march across the forest floor, millions of other insects flee in terror!
creatures.exploration_trait: Living Cable (Forms hanging ant-ropes down cliffs that the player can climb up and down).
creatures.visual_notes: Fierce curved ivory-jawed soldier with a pale golden head, mahogany abdomen, and hooked climbing claws.

creatures.name: Gold-Orchid
creatures.education: Male orchid bees are master perfume collectors! They visit rare jungle orchids, scrape aromatic fragrant oils onto their spongy hind legs, and mix them together into a custom cologne perfume that attracts a mate. Without these bees, thousands of orchids would vanish!
creatures.exploration_trait: Perfume Trail (Follows aromatic scents in the wind directly to rare hidden botanical ingredients).
creatures.visual_notes: Brilliant metallic emerald-green and turquoise bee with oversized swollen hind legs packed with golden pollen.

creatures.name: Pepsis
creatures.education: The tarantula hawk is a giant wasp with bright rust-orange wings. It specifically hunts giant tarantulas! It wrestles the spider, flips it over, and stings it to paralyze it. Her sting is so intensely painful that scientists advise anyone stung to just lie down and scream!
creatures.exploration_trait: Venom Neutralizer (Collects medicinal wasp enzymes that cure paralysis and venom debuffs).
creatures.visual_notes: Glossy blue-black metallic body with fiery blazing orange wings and hooked grasping legs.

creatures.name: Velveteen
creatures.education: Velvet ants aren't ants at all—they are wingless female wasps covered in bright fuzzy velvet hair! Their armor exoskeleton is so thick and slippery that entomologists have trouble pinning them with steel needles, and their sting is legendary for its power.
creatures.exploration_trait: Unbreakable Chitin (Shields the player from falling debris and sharp cacti spikes).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump adorable creature covered in velvety scarlet-orange and pitch-black fuzz with an armor under-chassis.

creatures.name: Assassin-Spike
creatures.education: Some species of assassin bugs in the rainforest glue the empty dried shells of their past insect meals onto their own backs! This tower of discarded bug armor acts as visual camouflage and confuses jumping spiders that try to attack them from behind.
creatures.exploration_trait: Armor Stacking (Collects crafting salvage and stacks it onto backpack frames for bonus inventory space).
creatures.visual_notes: Spiny stick-like body adorned with a curious backpack mound of hollow bug carapaces and a curved beak.

creatures.name: Harlequin-Beetle
creatures.education: The male harlequin beetle has front legs that are twice as long as its entire body! He uses these crazy long arms like a tightrope walker to navigate slippery tree bark and to fight rival males for the best sap-dripping branches.
creatures.exploration_trait: Long-Reach Pluck (Uses elongated forelegs to pluck fruit and items dangling from high canopy vines).
creatures.visual_notes: Stunning intricate Mayan-like red, black, and sage-green geometric patterns with comically long front legs.

creatures.name: Thorn-Hopper
creatures.education: Thorn bugs look exactly like the sharp green rose thorns on a jungle bush. Mother thorn bugs are wonderfully protective: when a predator approaches her babies, she vibrates her body against the plant stem to send an alarm signal through the wood to gather her young!
creatures.exploration_trait: Thorn Disguise (Allows companions to blend seamlessly into thorn bushes to bypass territorial beasts).
creatures.visual_notes: Vibrant emerald-green triangular insect shaped like a razor-sharp rose thorn with yellow racing stripes.

creatures.name: Glasswing
creatures.education: The glasswing butterfly has completely clear, transparent wings like glass windows! The tissue between its wing veins lacks colored scales, letting the forest foliage show right through. This makes them practically invisible when flying through dappled sunlight.
creatures.exploration_trait: Invisibility Cloak (Grants brief visual stealth to the player when sneaking past patrolling wildlife).
creatures.visual_notes: Crystal-clear glass wings framed in velvety chocolate brown and orange, with white horizontal racing bars.

creatures.name: Rhinocorn
creatures.education: Hercules beetles can lift up to 850 times their own body weight! That's the equivalent of a human lifting 10 full-sized school buses! In humid weather, their greenish-yellow wing covers actually change color to pitch black to absorb moisture.
creatures.exploration_trait: Pincer Hydraulic (Lifts fallen stone columns and jammed iron portcullises in jungle ruins).
creatures.visual_notes: Magnificent olive-yellow shell spotted with black, and an enormous pair of pincer horns lined with golden velvet.

creatures.name: Glowworm-Rail
creatures.education: The railroad worm looks like a train running at night! It has eleven pairs of glowing yellow-green lights along the sides of its body, and a bright red light on its head like a locomotive lantern! It is one of the only creatures that can produce true red bioluminescent light.
creatures.exploration_trait: Dual-Beam Lantern (Red light reveals hidden nocturnal wildlife without startling them; green illuminates paths).
creatures.visual_notes: Segmented caterpillar-like beetle larva glowing with ruby headlamps and jade side-window beacons.

creatures.name: Wander-Silk
creatures.education: Wandering spiders don't spin webs to catch food—they actively wander the jungle floor at night like tiny eight-legged ninjas. When cornered, they stand up tall on their back four legs, raise their front legs high in the air, and sway from side to side in a warning dance!
creatures.exploration_trait: Agile Strut (Detects micro-vibrations in the ground, alerting the player to approaching underground tunneling beasts).
creatures.visual_notes: Leggy fawn-brown hunting spider with bright red sensory hairs around its formidable fangs.

creatures.name: Deadleaf-Kat
creatures.education: The dead-leaf katydid is the ultimate camouflage artist! Its wings don't just look like a dead brown leaf—they have fake fungal mold spots, fake decay holes, and realistic leaf veins. Even hungry birds walking inches away cannot tell it apart from dead foliage!
creatures.exploration_trait: Decay Camouflage (Can disguise the player's camp tent as a natural leaf heap to prevent nocturnal raids).
creatures.visual_notes: Papery crinkled brown body shaped with ragged dry edges, bite marks, and microscopic faux-fungus speckles.

creatures.name: Giga-Pede
creatures.habitat: Cave Ceilings, Tree Hollows & Leaf Litter
creatures.education: Growing over a foot long, this is the largest centipede in the world! They are famous for hanging upside down from cave ceilings by their back legs, catching flying bats right out of the air with their front venom claws!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ceiling Crawl (Can walk upside-down along stone cave roofs and retrieve stalactite treasures).
creatures.visual_notes: Polished mahogany-red armored segments with bright yellow running legs and menacing dark forcipule fangs.

creatures.name: Heli-Damselfly
creatures.education: With a wingspan of over 7.5 inches, this is the largest damselfly on Earth! They hover in mid-air like tiny helicopters, spot spiders sitting in their webs, and pluck them out backwards with razor-spined feet without ever getting tangled in the sticky silk!
creatures.exploration_trait: Precision Hover (Hovers stationary in high winds to harvest delicate canopy blossoms without damaging them).
creatures.visual_notes: Incredibly long needle-like metallic blue abdomen and four shimmering paddle-wings tipped in bright yellow.

creatures.name: Bark-Mantis
creatures.habitat: Trunks of Massive Amazonian Hardwood Trees
creatures.education: Bark mantises are completely flat and patterned like tree lichen! Unlike other mantises that wait patiently, bark mantises sprint at lightning speed around tree trunks like tiny squirrels to chase down fleeing bugs.
creatures.exploration_trait: Trunk Sprint (Enables fast vertical climbing on sheer tree trunks without slipping).
creatures.visual_notes: Mottled moss-green and bark-gray flattened body with enormous pale green stereoscopic eyes.

creatures.name: Wax-Lantern
creatures.education: These insects secrete a fluffy, snow-white waxy powder from their tails that trails behind them like gossamer silk ribbons. If a bird grabs their tail, the wax breaks off cleanly in the bird's mouth, letting the insect fly safely away!
creatures.exploration_trait: Wax Sealant (Harvests waterproof waxy secretions used to craft water-resistant gear and tents).
creatures.visual_notes: Curved golden snout with trailing plumes of delicate, snow-white wax silk streamers.

creatures.name: Stingless-Mel
creatures.habitat: Hollow Ceiba Trees & Deep Rainforest Canopies
creatures.education: Amazonian stingless bees don't sting at all! Instead, they defend their hives by sealing intruders with sticky tree resin and clay. Their honey has been harvested by indigenous forest peoples for thousands of years as a miraculous natural antibiotic wound healer.
creatures.exploration_trait: Medicinal Honeycomb (Produces rare golden honey that restores companion vigor and cures poison states).
creatures.visual_notes: Gentle furry golden-black bee with sapphire blue compound eyes and sticky golden pollen baskets.

creatures.name: Dart-Toxin
creatures.education: The golden poison frog is the most toxic animal on planet Earth! A tiny two-inch frog has enough batrachotoxin venom on its skin to protect it from all predators and could stop ten adult humans! Indigenous hunters gently wipe blowgun dart tips across its back for hunting.
creatures.exploration_trait: Toxic Immunity (Provides passive immunity to poisonous swamp gas and toxic plant spores).
creatures.visual_notes: Radiant monochrome golden-yellow frog with large inky black eyes and a gleaming moist sheen.

creatures.name: Glassbell
creatures.education: Glass frogs have transparent skin on their bellies! If you look underneath them, you can see their beating red heart, stomach, and blood vessels working like a clear clockwork toy! They lay eggs on the undersides of leaves hanging directly over raging rivers.
creatures.exploration_trait: Vitals Sense (Detects the health status and elemental weaknesses of wild creatures before battle).
creatures.visual_notes: Translucent lime-green body with a clear crystal belly revealing a softly pulsing heart.

creatures.name: Surinam-Brood
creatures.habitat: Muddy Amazon Basin Riverbeds & Slow Creeks
creatures.education: The Surinam toad looks like a soggy dead leaf flattened on the riverbed! Mother toads have honeycombed skin on their backs: eggs sink right into her skin, and when the baby toadlets are fully grown, they pop right out of her back into the water!
creatures.exploration_trait: Mudbed Blend (Allows the player to camouflage inside muddy river shallows to observe shy fish).
creatures.visual_notes: Completely flat pancake-shaped gray-brown toad with star-shaped sensory fingertip pads.

creatures.name: Anacondra
creatures.education: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake on planet Earth, weighing up to 550 pounds! Their eyes and nostrils sit on top of their head so they can breathe and watch for prey while their massive muscular body remains completely hidden underwater.
creatures.exploration_trait: Swamp Drag (Can drag heavy submerged salvage, sunken logs, and river wreckage out of waterways).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal olive-green serpent patterned with dark oval spots and yellow belly scales.

creatures.name: Tree-Emerald
creatures.education: Emerald tree boas have giant curved teeth longer than almost any non-venomous snake! When resting, they coil in a neat saddle knot over a horizontal tree branch with their head tucked right in the center. Babies are born bright brick-red and turn emerald green as they grow!
creatures.exploration_trait: Saddle Coil (Creates safe secure hammock anchor points in the canopy for resting).
creatures.visual_notes: Brilliant emerald-green scales marked with lightning-bolt white zigzags and pale lemon belly.

creatures.name: Bushmaster-Fang
creatures.habitat: Pristine Primary Rainforests & Deep Leaf Litter
creatures.education: The bushmaster is the longest venomous snake in the Americas, growing over 11 feet long! The scientific name 'Lachesis' comes from the Greek Fate who cuts the thread of life. Unlike other pit vipers that give live birth, bushmasters lay eggs and coil around them to guard them.
creatures.exploration_trait: Pit-Organ Thermal (Detects warm-blooded creatures hidden behind wooden walls and dense bushes).
creatures.visual_notes: Tough pinkish-tan body marked with bold dark chocolate diamond saddles and keeled pineapple scales.

creatures.name: Caimano-Black
creatures.habitat: Slow Amazon River Channels, Oxbow Lakes
creatures.education: The black caiman can grow over 16 feet long—the true king of the Amazon's waterways! Their dark, armored skin absorbs heat from the tropical sun during the day, keeping them warm and energetic during night-time hunts.
creatures.exploration_trait: Oxbow Ferry (Transports player and heavy party members across predator-packed blackwater lakes).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy black scuted armor plates with pale yellow belly bands and glowing predatory golden eyes.

creatures.name: Yacare-Shield
creatures.education: The Pantanal is home to over 10 million yacare caimans! They have teeth that stick outside their lower jaw like a toothy grin, earning them the nickname 'piranha caiman' because they feast on schools of piranhas, keeping fish numbers balanced.
creatures.exploration_trait: Marsh Dredger (Clears choked wetland waterways of dense water hyacinths and debris).
creatures.visual_notes: Olive-brown hide with dark blotches, visible lower teeth, and a grinning armored snout.

creatures.name: Jesus-Stride
creatures.education: The green basilisk lizard can literally walk on water! When frightened, it drops from a tree and sprints on its back legs across river surfaces at 5 feet per second! Special fringe scales on its toes trap bubbles of air that keep it from sinking.
creatures.exploration_trait: Water Sprint (Allows the player to sprint across open water surfaces for short durations without drowning).
creatures.visual_notes: Brilliant emerald-green lizard with regal head crests, back sails, and long fringed toe scales.

creatures.name: Matamata
creatures.education: The mata mata turtle looks like a pile of rotting bark with a snorkel! It has a long tubular nose that sticks out of the water like a straw, and when a fish swims near, it opens its giant mouth so fast that the rush of water vacuums the fish straight inside!
creatures.exploration_trait: Vacuum Suction (Vacuums up loose floating debris, sunken seeds, and river treasure from deep pools).
creatures.visual_notes: Rough bark-like shell with three knobby keels, flat triangular head, and fringed skin flaps.

creatures.name: Piranhaw
creatures.education: Piranhas aren't the mindless movie monsters people think they are! They mostly eat fallen seeds, fruit, and sick fish. Their razor-sharp triangular teeth interlock like scissors, and indigenous people historically used their jawbones to cut hair and carve wood!
creatures.exploration_trait: Submerged Cleaver (Can chew through tough submerged wooden pilings and sunken roots).
creatures.visual_notes: Shimmering silver body with fiery red throat and belly, bulldog jaw, and razor-sharp white teeth.

creatures.name: Volt-Eel
creatures.education: The electric eel is actually a knifefish, not a true eel! It can produce an incredible electrical shock of up to 860 volts—the strongest biological electrical discharge on Earth! It also uses gentle low-voltage clicks like an underwater sonar radar.
creatures.exploration_trait: Bio-Generator (Powers up ancient electric mechanisms, conduits, and submersible generators).
creatures.visual_notes: Long cylindrical slate-gray knifefish with glowing electric organ lines and a broad orange throat.

creatures.name: Pirarucu
creatures.diet: Fish, Birds, Small Monkeys jumping near water
creatures.education: The arapaima is an ancient living fossil that can grow over 10 feet long and weigh 400 pounds! Because jungle floodwaters often lack oxygen, it must surface every 15 minutes to breathe air through a primitive lung that makes a loud coughing gulp!
creatures.exploration_trait: Titan River Mount (Rideable aquatic behemoth capable of carrying the player through floodplains).
creatures.visual_notes: Streamlined torpedo body with mineral-hard scales tipped in fiery ruby-red and a bony armored skull.

creatures.name: Boto-Pink
creatures.habitat: Amazon & Orinoco River Systems & Flooded Forests
creatures.education: The boto is famous for turning bright bubblegum pink as it grows older! Unlike ocean dolphins whose neck bones are fused, the boto can turn its head 90 degrees to maneuver gracefully through underwater tree trunks in the flooded jungle during rainy season.
creatures.exploration_trait: Flooded Forest Navigator (Guides the player through submerged treetop mazes during flood seasons).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump friendly dolphin with soft rosy-pink skin, long slender beak, bulbous forehead melon, and low dorsal ridge.

creatures.name: Podocnemis
creatures.species: Giant South American River Turtle / Arrau
creatures.diet: Fallen Forest Fruit, Seeds, Aquatic Plants
creatures.education: The arrau is the largest freshwater turtle in South America, weighing over 150 pounds! Mother turtles communicate with their babies while they are still inside their eggs using low-frequency clicking vocalizations beneath the sand to time their hatching together!
creatures.exploration_trait: Sandbank Sifter (Locates buried river pearls, mineral sands, and rare river treasures).
creatures.visual_notes: Smooth broad dark-olive carapace with yellow facial markings and large paddle-like webbed flippers.

creatures.name: Harpy-Talon
creatures.habitat: Canopy of Undisturbed Tropical Lowland Forests
creatures.education: The harpy eagle is one of the most powerful eagles in the world! Its back talons can be over five inches long—larger than the claws of a grizzly bear! They can exert over 500 pounds of pressure per square inch, effortlessly snatching a sloth right out of a tall canopy tree.
creatures.exploration_trait: Apex Glide (Soars above the dense rainforest canopy to survey map territory and locate rare beasts).
creatures.visual_notes: Regal double-crested feather crown, slate-black back mantle, pure white breast, and terrifying golden talons.

creatures.name: Toco-Bill
creatures.diet: Figs, Palm Nuts, Insects, Tree Eggs
creatures.education: The toucan's bill looks heavy, but it is actually super lightweight and hollow, reinforced with a honeycomb of keratin struts like an airplane wing! It acts as a natural air conditioner: the bird pumps blood into its beak to release body heat and cool down on hot jungle days.
creatures.exploration_trait: Canopy Forager (Reaches into tight tree hollows to harvest rare tropical seeds and palm fruit).
creatures.visual_notes: Glossy black body, snow-white throat bib, and an enormous rainbow-orange bill tipped with a black oval.

creatures.name: Scarlet-Wing
creatures.diet: Toxic Seeds, Brazil Nuts, Clay from Riverbanks
creatures.education: Macaws can live for over 50 years and mate for life! They have jaw muscles so strong they can easily crack rock-hard Brazil nut shells. In the Amazon, flocks gather at clay licks to eat mineral-rich clay, which binds to toxins in wild seeds and keeps their bellies healthy.
creatures.exploration_trait: Clay Lick Scout (Locates mineral clay banks that produce healing stomach draughts and ceramics).
creatures.visual_notes: Blazing scarlet plumage with bright yellow and electric blue wing bands and long streaming scarlet tail feathers.

creatures.name: Hoatzin-Claw
creatures.diet: Leaves of Arum Plants & Mangrove Foliage
creatures.education: The hoatzin is one of the weirdest birds on Earth! Its chicks are born with dinosaur-like claws on their wings that let them climb up tree branches. It digests leaves in a special fermentation crop just like a cow, which gives it a funny manure smell, earning the nickname 'stinkbird'!
creatures.exploration_trait: Wing-Claw Climb (Allows companion to scale steep wooden river pilings and knotted rope ladders).
creatures.visual_notes: Wild unkempt rufous-and-buff mohawk crest, bright blue bare facial skin, ruby eyes, and wing-tip claws.

creatures.name: Sword-Hummer
creatures.education: The sword-billed hummingbird is the ONLY bird in the world whose bill is longer than the rest of its entire body (excluding tail)! It evolved this needle-like beak specifically to drink nectar from hanging trumpet passionflowers that no other bird can reach.
creatures.exploration_trait: Needle Pluck (Extracts rare nectar and crystal dew from deep, narrow crevices in rock walls).
creatures.visual_notes: Glittering bronze-green plumage with an astonishing long slender bill pointing forward like a fencing foil.

creatures.name: Oilbird-Echo
creatures.education: Oilbirds are the only nocturnal fruit-eating flying birds in the world! They roost inside pitch-black caves by day and use echolocation—clicking soundwaves just like bats and dolphins—to navigate through dark subterranean caverns without crashing into stalactites.
creatures.exploration_trait: Sonar Ping (Maps out pitch-black cave networks and reveals hidden subterranean paths).
creatures.visual_notes: Rich chestnut-brown plumage dotted with white diamond spots, hooked bill with sensory facial whiskers.

creatures.name: Andes-Condor
creatures.habitat: High Andes Mountains & Pacific Sea Cliffs
creatures.diet: Carrion of Guanacos, Deer, Sea Mammals
creatures.education: With a wingspan of over 10.5 feet, the Andean condor is one of the largest flying birds in the world! They can soar for over 100 miles across the Andes mountains without flapping their wings once, riding mountain thermal updrafts like an majestic glider plane.
creatures.exploration_trait: High-Peak Thermal (Can carry the player to soaring mountain peaks and windy alpine passes).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive black wings with snowy-white wing bars, a fluffy white neck ruff collar, and regal caruncle head crest.

creatures.name: Sunbittern-Eye
creatures.habitat: Shaded Stream Margins in Wet Forests
creatures.education: Normally, the sunbittern looks like a shy brown bird walking quietly along stream gravel. But when a predator approaches, it fans open its wings to reveal two enormous, radiant red-and-gold sunset 'eyes' that look like the face of a giant mountain predator!
creatures.exploration_trait: Solar Flash Ward (Flashes wing eyespots to scare off territorial carnivores and avoid combat).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender neck with banded plumage that fans out into magnificent sunset-colored eye-spot wing shields.

creatures.name: Jabiru-Stork
creatures.diet: Fish, Frogs, Water Snakes, Small Caimans
creatures.education: The jabiru is the tallest flying bird in South America, standing nearly five feet tall! Its name means 'swollen neck' in Tupi-Guarani, because its bare red throat patch swells with air when excited. Their massive stick nests in solitary trees are used for generations.
creatures.exploration_trait: Wetland Lookout (Marks distant shallow wadeable passages across flooded marsh maps).
creatures.visual_notes: Stately pure-white body with an unfeathered jet-black neck, bright scarlet throat ring, and heavy upturned bill.

creatures.name: Piha-Screamer
creatures.education: The screaming piha is the true voice of the Amazon! Almost every jungle movie you've ever seen uses its piercing, whistling call as background sound. The bird is small and plain gray, but its call can reach 116 decibels—louder than a rock concert!
creatures.exploration_trait: Sonic Echo (Triggers acoustic resonance bells and shatters fragile crystal caverns).
creatures.visual_notes: Modest ash-gray forest bird with a wide singing bill and an unexpectedly powerful vocal resonance sac.

creatures.name: Cock-o-the-Rock
creatures.education: The male cock-of-the-rock looks like a fiery orange sunburst! His entire head is crowned with a half-moon fan crest that completely hides his bill. Groups of males gather in special forest clearings called 'leks' to display their vibrant feathers on mossy boulders.
creatures.exploration_trait: Lek Dance Beacon (Attracts rare wildlife species to gathering points for discovery and cataloging).
creatures.visual_notes: Blazing neon-orange plumage with a half-moon disc crest framing the face, black wings edged in white silk.

creatures.name: Potoo-Stump
creatures.habitat: Lowland Forest Canopies & High Dead Branches
creatures.education: The potoo is the undisputed champion of tree mimicry! By day, it perches on a broken dead branch, points its bill straight up, and freezes completely motionless. Its bark-colored feathers make it look like part of the wooden stump! It even has tiny slits in its eyelids to peek with eyes closed.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stump Stand (Becomes completely undetectable by predators while resting at camp).
creatures.visual_notes: Mottled grey-and-buff plumage mimicking dead wood bark, huge yellow nocturnal eyes, and gaping wide mouth.

creatures.name: Burrow-Owl
creatures.education: Unlike most owls that live high in trees, burrowing owls live underground in burrows dug by armadillos! When threatened inside their burrow, young owls make a hissing rattling sound that sounds exactly like a venomous rattlesnake to scare invaders away!
creatures.exploration_trait: Burrow Sentry (Warns of underground cave-ins and alerts the player to subterranean treasure dens).
creatures.visual_notes: Long-legged mottled brown owl with bright lemon-yellow eyes, white chin bib, and inquisitive head tilts.

creatures.name: Rhea-Runner
creatures.education: The rhea is the largest bird in South America! Father rheas are super-dads: the male builds the nest, incubates all the eggs laid by multiple females, and bravely guards up to 30 young chicks on his own, fiercely chasing away any danger!
creatures.exploration_trait: Pampas Sprint (Fast ground mount across flat grassland terrain with swift zig-zag dodging).
creatures.visual_notes: Tall flightless bird with shaggy gray-brown plumage, strong three-toed running legs, and alert dark eyes.

creatures.name: King-Cowl
creatures.education: The king vulture gets royal treatment from other scavengers! When a king vulture lands at a feast, smaller vultures step aside and wait for the king to eat first. Ancient Mayan mythology believed this magnificent bird was a messenger between humans and the gods.
creatures.exploration_trait: Royal Presence (Intimidates small scavenging critters away from camp supplies).
creatures.visual_notes: Creamy-white body with black wing-tips, pure white eyes, and a brightly colored head with orange and purple wattles.

creatures.name: Spix-Azure
creatures.habitat: Arid Caatinga Scrub & Caraibeira River Woods
creatures.diet: Seeds and Nuts of Pinhão & Caraibeira Trees
creatures.education: The Spix's macaw is one of the rarest and most famous birds on Earth—the real-life inspiration for the movie 'Rio'! Once declared extinct in the wild, dedicated conservationists and scientists have bred them in protected sanctuaries and are successfully returning them to their wild homeland!
creatures.exploration_trait: Sanctuary Bond (Increases the sanctuary happiness and breeding recovery rate of all companions).
creatures.visual_notes: Stunning monochrome cyan-and-periwinkle plumage with light smoky-blue facial feathers and charcoal bill.

creatures.name: Golden-Conure
creatures.diet: Canopy Seeds, Wild Fruit, Flowers, Maize
creatures.education: The golden parakeet is painted in the national colors of Brazil—pure brilliant yellow plumage with contrasting dark green flight feathers! They are incredibly social and cooperative, with several adult pairs happily helping to feed and raise a single clutch of chicks.
creatures.exploration_trait: Cooperative Chirp (Reduces the resource crafting costs of homestead upgrades).
creatures.visual_notes: Radiant buttercup-yellow body accented with emerald-green primary flight wings and dark expressive eyes.

creatures.name: Agami-Heron
creatures.habitat: Dense Swamp Forests & Shaded Stream Margins
creatures.education: Often called the 'miracle of the swamps,' the agami heron is one of the most secretive and beautiful waterbirds on Earth. Unlike other tall herons, it has short legs and stays deep in shadowy thickets over water, using its dagger beak to strike like lightning.
creatures.exploration_trait: Shadow Wade (Can wade silently through swamp waters without rippling the surface or alerting fish).
creatures.visual_notes: Glossy bottle-green back, chestnut belly, delicate pale-blue neck crest plumes, and yellow dagger bill.

creatures.name: Caracara-Scout
creatures.education: The crested caracara is a falcon that walks and runs on the ground like a rooster! They are curious problem solvers that flip over dried cow patties and river stones with their feet to catch hidden beetles and crabs.
creatures.exploration_trait: Stone Flipper (Flips over riverbed flagstones to discover hidden coins, fossils, and rare minerals).
creatures.visual_notes: Regal black cap crest, finely barred black-and-white neck, red facial skin, and long yellow running legs.

creatures.name: Andes-Flamingo
creatures.habitat: High Altitude Salt Lakes & Salar Lagoons
creatures.education: These hardy flamingos live in freezing salt lakes high up in the Andes mountains, over 12,000 feet above sea level! They get their lovely pink color from eating microscopic algae rich in carotenoid pigments. They are the only flamingo with bright yellow legs!
creatures.exploration_trait: Salt Flat Stride (Traverses corrosive alkali salt flats and mineral crags without footwear damage).
creatures.visual_notes: Pale pink body with deep crimson neck streaks, black wing triangle, and distinctive bright yellow legs.

creatures.name: Cappy
creatures.education: The capybara is the largest rodent in the world, weighing up to 150 pounds! They are famous for being the friendliest creatures in the wild: birds, monkeys, and even turtles love sitting on their backs while they take relaxing mud baths. They can stay underwater for five minutes!
creatures.exploration_trait: Peaceful Aura (Pacifies nearby wild creatures and prevents aggressive encounters while resting).
creatures.visual_notes: Stout barrel-shaped body with coarse reddish-brown hair, blunt friendly snout, and partially webbed feet.

creatures.name: Anteater-Snout
creatures.diet: Ants & Termites (eats up to 30,000 a day!)
creatures.education: The giant anteater has no teeth at all! Instead, it has a tongue that is two feet long and covered in thousands of tiny backward-pointing microscopic hooks and sticky saliva. It can flick its tongue in and out of termite mounds over 150 times per minute!
creatures.exploration_trait: Termite Breaker (Shatters rock-solid termite concrete with curved front claws to reveal minerals).
creatures.visual_notes: Elongated tubular snout, bold diagonal black-and-white shoulder stripe, and a giant shaggy feather-duster tail.

creatures.name: Silky-Claw
creatures.education: The silky anteater is the smallest anteater in the world—it weighs less than a can of soup! Covered in golden silky fur that looks like cotton tree seedpods, it spends its whole life up in trees. When startled, it stands on its hind legs and raises its claws in a boxer stance!
creatures.exploration_trait: Canopy Snuggle (Can squeeze through tiny tree knotholes to retrieve lost keys and trinkets).
creatures.visual_notes: Fluffy golden-yellow plush body with prehensile tail and two tiny curved climbing claws on each hand.

creatures.name: Sloth-Slow
creatures.education: Sloths move so slowly that real green algae actually grows inside their fur! This turns their coat green, providing perfect natural camouflage among leaves. A whole tiny community of specialized sloth moths and harmless beetles lives inside a sloth's fur coat!
creatures.exploration_trait: Algal Camouflage (Blends into green canopies, reducing player threat level to zero).
creatures.visual_notes: Shaggy greenish-brown coat, perpetual peaceful smiling face with dark eye mask, and three curved hook claws.

creatures.name: Pygmy-Marmoset
creatures.education: The pygmy marmoset is the smallest monkey in the world! As adults, they weigh less than an orange and can fit right on a human finger. They have specialized front teeth that gnaw tiny holes into tree bark to make the tree bleed sweet, gummy sap for breakfast.
creatures.exploration_trait: Sap Tapper (Taps rubber trees and sweet gums for valuable crafting adhesives and tonics).
creatures.visual_notes: Tiny tawny-gold fur ball with a ringed balancing tail, lion-like mane ruff, and curious inquisitive eyes.

creatures.name: Tamarin-Mane
creatures.diet: Fruit, Flower Nectar, Tree Frogs, Insects
creatures.education: The golden lion tamarin gets its name from its breathtaking, radiant golden mane that frames its dark face like a miniature African lion! They communicate through sweet, high-pitched trills that sound like songbirds singing in the morning mist.
creatures.exploration_trait: Canopy Acrobat (Swings through tangled liana vine vines to drop shortcut ropes for the player).
creatures.visual_notes: Breathtaking silky mane of pure spun gold with tiny agile fingers and dark curious eyes.

creatures.name: Howler-Bellow
creatures.education: Howler monkeys are the loudest land animals in the Americas! They have an enlarged, hollow U-shaped hyoid bone in their throat that acts as a natural sound amplifier. Their roaring barks can be heard clearly three miles away through thick jungle!
creatures.exploration_trait: Megaphone Roar (Disrupts enemy battle formations and triggers echo resonances in mountain passes).
creatures.visual_notes: Solid midnight-black fur on males with a massive throat pouch and strong prehensile grasping tail.

creatures.name: Emperor-Moustache
creatures.diet: Fruit, Tree Sap, Flower Nectar, Tree Frogs
creatures.education: The emperor tamarin has a magnificent, sweeping white handlebar mustache that extends past its shoulders! Legend says German scientists named it as a joke after the German Emperor Wilhelm II, who had a famously groomed mustache.
creatures.exploration_trait: Mustache Charm (Unlocks unique diplomatic responses and peaceful trade with tribal forest NPCs).
creatures.visual_notes: Mottled grey coat, reddish-orange tail, and an enormous snowy-white handlebar mustache.

creatures.name: Coati-Snout
creatures.education: Coatis are cousins of raccoons, but they are daytime wanderers with long, flexible, upturned snouts! They walk with their long ringed tails held straight up in the air like antennas so troop members don't lose each other in tall forest ferns.
creatures.exploration_trait: Snout Forager (Sniffs out rare buried truffles, wild tubers, and hidden relic caches).
creatures.visual_notes: Warm reddish-amber coat with white snout mask, long striped tail held upright, and flexible pig-like nose.

creatures.name: Kinkajou-Tail
creatures.diet: Wild Honey, Ripe Fruit, Flower Nectar
creatures.education: The kinkajou is affectionately known as the 'honey bear' because it raids wild bee hives with a five-inch prehensile tongue to lick up golden honey! It can rotate its back ankles 180 degrees backwards to run down tree trunks face-first!
creatures.exploration_trait: Tree-Trunk Reverse (Can scale down vertical cliff faces and trees head-first without falling).
creatures.visual_notes: Golden-brown velvety fur with large dark nocturnal eyes, round ears, and a strong wrapping prehensile tail.

creatures.name: Ocelot-Gleam
creatures.habitat: Dense Brush, Mangrove Swamps & Lowland Forest
creatures.education: The ocelot has one of the most beautiful coats in nature, covered in chains of golden rosettes rimmed in velvet black. Unlike housecats, ocelots love water! They are skilled swimmers and love splashing through shallow riverbeds to catch fish.
creatures.exploration_trait: Silent Stalker (Moves completely silently through crunchy underbrush without making noise).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek muscular small feline with chain-like golden rosettes, white eye bars, and luminous amber eyes.

creatures.name: Margay-Branch
creatures.diet: Tree Frogs, Birds, Squirrels, Tree Rats
creatures.education: The margay is the most acrobatic cat on planet Earth! It can hang upside down from a tree branch by just one back foot like an acrobat monkey, and it can vocalize mimics of baby tamarin monkey cries to lure curious prey into range!
creatures.exploration_trait: Acrobatic Hang (Allows one-handed hanging from ropes and ledges to perform complex actions).
creatures.visual_notes: Large liquid nocturnal eyes, soft spotted gold coat, and broad clawed paws built for tree branches.

creatures.name: Bushdog-Pack
creatures.education: Bush dogs look like little stocky badger-dogs with webbed toes! They hunt in tight-knit family packs that communicate with sweet bird-like squeaks. They are incredible swimmers and can dive underwater to chase aquatic rodents like pacas!
creatures.exploration_trait: Pack Squeak (Boosts the party's movement speed and coordination when traveling through swamps).
creatures.visual_notes: Stocky reddish-tan dog with short legs, stubby tail, badger-like ears, and webbed paws.

creatures.name: Stilt-Wolf
creatures.education: The maned wolf looks like a golden fox on stilts! Its super-long black legs evolved to let it see over tall cerrado grass. Over half of its diet is a wild tomato-like fruit called the 'wolf apple,' which protects its kidneys from parasites!
creatures.exploration_trait: Stilt Stride (Walks easily through high marsh grass and flooded reedbeds without slowing down).
creatures.visual_notes: Golden-red coat, dramatic black mane along neck, snowy white throat bib, and remarkably long black legs.

creatures.name: Tayra-Weasel
creatures.diet: Wild Honey, Fruit, Lizards, Small Rodents
creatures.education: The tayra is an ultra-smart jungle weasel that actually plans for the future! Scientists observed tayras picking unripe green plantains and caching them in safe tree forks until the fruit ripened to a sweet yellow before returning to feast!
creatures.exploration_trait: Ripening Cache (Stores picked wild fruit in camp caches that passively upgrade into rare culinary treats).
creatures.visual_notes: Long dark brown muscular body with a distinctive cream throat patch, bushy tail, and curious rounded face.

creatures.name: Chinchilla-Fur
creatures.education: Chinchillas have the densest fur of any land mammal—with 50 to 80 individual hairs growing out of a single follicle (humans have just one)! Their fur is so dense that water cannot penetrate it, so they bathe in fine volcanic dust to stay clean and fluffy.
creatures.exploration_trait: Volcanic Dust Cleanse (Neutralizes toxic status effects and cleans player gear using volcanic ash).
creatures.visual_notes: Incredibly fluffy silver-gray fur ball with giant round velvety ears and squirrel-like plumed tail.

creatures.name: Pudu-Mini
creatures.habitat: Temperate Rainforests & Bamboo Belts of the Andes
creatures.education: The pudu is the smallest deer in the world, standing only 14 inches tall at the shoulder! Because they are so tiny, they climb over fallen logs, scramble up slanted tree trunks, and bend down tall bamboo stalks by climbing onto them to reach tender green leaves.
creatures.exploration_trait: Bamboo Tunnel (Squeezes through dense bamboo tunnels inaccessible to humans to find secret clearings).
creatures.visual_notes: Round chestnut-brown miniature deer with tiny spiky antlers, button nose, and gentle dark eyes.

creatures.name: Pacarana-Chub
creatures.habitat: Rainforest Slopes & Valleys of the Andes
creatures.education: The pacarana is the third largest rodent on Earth, weighing up to 30 pounds! The scientific name means 'terrible mouse,' but it is actually a gentle, slow-moving vegetarian that uses its agile human-like front paws to hold fruit while dining peacefully.
creatures.exploration_trait: Root Harvester (Digs up tough underground highland tubers and medicinal roots without damaging them).
creatures.visual_notes: Chubby dark brown rodent with double white stripes along its back, white polka dots, and blunt whiskered nose.

creatures.name: Armadillo-Giant
creatures.education: The giant armadillo weighs up to 110 pounds and has a massive third claw that can reach eight inches long—the largest claw relative to body size of any living mammal! It can dig a burrow so large that a human can easily crawl inside it.
creatures.exploration_trait: Titan Claw Trench (Excavates deep subterranean shelter burrows that protect the player from sandstorms).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal armored carapace with flexible mid-body bands, pale yellowish skirt, and a giant sickle-like claw.

creatures.name: Nine-Banded
creatures.education: Nine-banded armadillos have an amazing aquatic trick! To cross a narrow creek, they sink to the bottom and simply walk across underwater. But to cross a wide river, they inflate their stomach and intestines with air to float like a biological rubber boat!
creatures.exploration_trait: Puff-Float (Floats like a buoyant buoy, allowing the player to tow supplies across broad lakes).
creatures.visual_notes: Armor carapace divided into nine flexible bands, pig-like snout, and defensive armor headcap.

creatures.name: Jaguara
creatures.education: The jaguar has the strongest bite force of any big cat on Earth! Unlike lions and tigers that bite the throat, the jaguar pierces straight through the thick armored skulls of caimans and hard shells of turtles with its crushing canine teeth! The name comes from 'yaguar,' meaning 'he who kills with one leap.'
creatures.exploration_trait: Apex Trample (Crushes through reinforced bone barricades and triggers ancient feline trial doors).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy muscular golden frame patterned with large rosettes centered with black dots, and piercing amber eyes.

creatures.name: Puma-Shadow
creatures.habitat: Andean Mountain Peaks, Patagonian Steppes & Forests
creatures.education: The puma holds the Guinness World Record for the animal with the highest number of different names (over 40 in English alone, including cougar, mountain lion, and panther)! They are Olympic jumpers: a puma can leap 40 feet forward in a single bound across mountain ravines!
creatures.exploration_trait: Chasm Leap (Leaps across wide mountain chasms and sheer cliff drops while mounted).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek tawny-fawn coat with pale throat, dark tail tip, powerful athletic shoulders, and icy green-gold eyes.

creatures.name: Spectacled-Bear
creatures.habitat: High Cloud Forests & Paramo Grasslands of the Andes
creatures.diet: Bromeliad Hearts, Palm Fruit, Bamboo, Cactus
creatures.education: The spectacled bear is the ONLY living species of bear native to South America! They build big leafy platform nests high up in trees where they sleep and feast on wild fruit. They get their name from distinctive golden rings around their eyes that look like eyeglasses!
creatures.exploration_trait: Canopy Nest Builder (Builds elevated treehouse platforms for high-altitude resting and surveillance).
creatures.visual_notes: Dense shaggy black fleece coat with distinctive creamy-yellow rings around its expressive eyes and snout.

creatures.name: Tapir-Lowland
creatures.education: The tapir is the largest native land mammal in South America! It has a short, flexible prehensile snout like a miniature elephant trunk that it uses to pluck fruit and leaves. When running through the jungle, it dives into deep rivers to escape jaguars!
creatures.exploration_trait: Submerged Plunge (Takes the player on deep river crossings, safely hidden beneath water lilies).
creatures.visual_notes: Heavy slate-gray body with a narrow raised neck crest mane, flexible trunk snout, and white ear tips.

creatures.name: Tapir-Mountain
creatures.habitat: High Altitude Paramo & Mist Cloud Forests
creatures.diet: Alpine Grasses, Ferns, High Mountain Bromeliads
creatures.education: Unlike its lowland cousin, the mountain tapir lives high in the misty Andes mountains and is covered in a thick, woolly fur coat to stay warm in freezing mountain rains! They have striking white lips and act as seed planters for high alpine flora.
creatures.exploration_trait: Alpine Pathfinder (Guides companions safely through freezing blizzard passes without hypothermia).
creatures.visual_notes: Dense woolly charcoal fleece coat with distinctive chalk-white lip borders and flexible prehensile snout.

creatures.name: Guanaco-Plains
creatures.habitat: Patagonian Steppes, Arid Scrub & Mountain Slopes
creatures.education: Guanacos are the wild ancestors of domestic llamas! They live in the windiest, harshest regions of South America. If another animal annoys a guanaco, it gives a high-pitched alarm laugh and accurately spits a burst of chewed grass and saliva from ten feet away!
creatures.exploration_trait: Gale Endurance (Provides immunity to heavy desert winds and sandstorm navigation penalties).
creatures.visual_notes: Elegant long-necked camelid with warm cinnamon fleece, white underparts, grey face, and dark gentle eyes.

creatures.name: Vicuna-Fleece
creatures.education: The vicuña produces the finest, warmest, and most valuable wool in the world! In the ancient Inca Empire, only the royal Inca emperor was permitted to wear garments woven from golden vicuña wool. They are wild, swift, and cannot be kept in captivity.
creatures.exploration_trait: Royal Fleece (Harvests ultra-insulating golden fleece used to craft high-tier extreme-weather outfits).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender delicate golden-fawn camelid with a long white bib of silky chest fleece and large liquid dark eyes.

creatures.name: Marsh-Stag
creatures.diet: Water Lilies, Marsh Grasses, Floating Flora
creatures.education: The marsh deer is the largest deer species in South America! They have specialized broad hooves with elastic interdigital webbing that splay wide open like snowshoes, allowing this massive stag to run across floating marsh reeds without sinking into mud!
creatures.exploration_trait: Reed Marsh Stride (Mounted speed across deep water marshes and floating reedbeds without sinking).
creatures.visual_notes: Magnificent reddish-chestnut stag with large branched antlers, black stockings on its legs, and white eye rings.

creatures.name: Otter-Giant
creatures.education: Growing up to six feet long, the giant otter is the longest weasel in the world! Known as the 'river wolf,' family groups are so coordinated and fearless that a pack of giant otters will actively chase down and fight large black caimans and anacondas!
creatures.exploration_trait: River Wolf Pack (Guarantees safe travel across predator-heavy riverways, scaring away aquatic alphas).
creatures.visual_notes: Sleek chocolate-brown velvet coat with unique cream throat patch, webbed paws, and flattened rudder tail.

creatures.name: Manatee-Amazon
creatures.habitat: Amazon River Basin Floodplains & Oxbow Lakes
creatures.education: The Amazonian manatee is the only species of manatee that lives strictly in freshwater! They have smooth rubbery skin and a bright white or pink patch on their chest. During dry seasons, they can fast for up to seven months, slowly digesting stored body fat!
creatures.exploration_trait: Weed Harvester (Clears vast waterways of invasive choking weeds to yield crafting fibers and fodder).
creatures.visual_notes: Plump rounded slate-gray river giant with paddle flippers, white chest emblem, and split whiskered muzzle.

creatures.name: Yacare-Titan
creatures.habitat: Deep Swamps of the Pantanal Heart
creatures.education: Ancient elder yacares that survive centuries in deep wetland sanctuaries grow into armored river monitors. Their thick bony skin plates are so heavily calcified that teeth and arrows bounce right off their armored backs.
creatures.exploration_trait: Submerged Bridge (Can rest in shallow gaps to act as a living stepping-stone bridge for the player).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal moss-encrusted black-and-gold caiman with ancient scarring and protruding jagged teeth.

creatures.name: Anaconda-Colossus
creatures.habitat: Deep Uncharted Swamps of the Orinoco Delta
creatures.education: Female green anacondas are up to five times larger than males! Elder matriarchs in pristine remote wetlands can reach mythical sizes, remaining submerged for hours while generating enough muscular constriction to crush giant boulders.
creatures.exploration_trait: Tidal Current Surge (Can part fast-moving river currents to reveal sunken ancient ruins).
creatures.visual_notes: Enormous muscular dark emerald serpent with thick black rosettes and iridescent river-sheen scales.

creatures.name: Jaguarundi-Fleet
creatures.habitat: Lowland Brush, Forest Margins & Swamp Edges
creatures.education: The jaguarundi looks like an otter crossed with a weasel, but it is a true wild cat related to the cougar! Unlike most cats, they are active in the middle of the day, communicate through 13 different bird-like chirps, and run with a low, slinking gallop.
creatures.exploration_trait: Low-Brush Sprint (Can sprint through tangled ground brush without catching or stumbling).
creatures.visual_notes: Slender unspotted reddish-chestnut coat with short legs, elongated weasel-like body, and small rounded ears.

creatures.name: Boto-Titan
creatures.habitat: Araguaia River Basin & Deep Lagoon Sanctuaries
creatures.diet: Armored Catfish, River Crabs, Riverine Prey
creatures.education: In Amazonian folklore, the pink river dolphin is a magical shapeshifter called the 'Encantado' that transforms into a handsome human wearing a straw hat to attend village celebrations! Biologically, they are crucial indicators of healthy, clean rivers.
creatures.exploration_trait: Encantado Chime (Unlocks mystical river shrine portals and purifies polluted water supplies).
creatures.visual_notes: Magnificent luminous rosy-pink river dolphin crowned with soft bioluminescent water glyphs.

creatures.name: Orinoco-Apex
creatures.habitat: Wide River Channels of the Orinoco Basin
creatures.diet: Large River Fish, Capybaras, Grazing Cattle
creatures.education: The Orinoco crocodile is one of the largest predators in the Americas, with historical males reaching over 20 feet in length! They have narrow, pale snouts designed to catch fast swimming river fish and can bellow so loudly the ground vibrates.
creatures.exploration_trait: Seismic Bellow (Emits a deep sub-audible vibration that crumbles cracked stone dam blockages).
creatures.visual_notes: Pale yellowish-tan armored giant with dark brown cross-banding and a long, formidable narrow snout.

creatures.name: Anteater-Titan
creatures.education: Elder giant anteaters with decades of wild foraging experience possess front claws strong enough to rip through sedimentary stone. Even jaguars will avoid fighting a fully-grown giant anteater standing on its hind legs in defensive posture.
creatures.exploration_trait: Bedrock Claws (Shatters tough geological rock strata to reveal hidden subterranean crystal geodes).
creatures.visual_notes: Massive shaggy gray-and-black anteater with reinforced stone-like claw plating and a billowing plume tail.

creatures.name: Andes-Cat
creatures.habitat: High Altitude Rocky Scree & Chinchilla Colonies
creatures.education: The Andean mountain cat is the most endangered cat in the Americas, with fewer than 2,500 individuals surviving high in the Andes! It has an enormous, fluffy, banded tail that is two-thirds as long as its entire body, which acts like a balancing pole and warm winter blanket.
creatures.exploration_trait: Scree Balance (Effortlessly traverses loose, sliding mountain shale and rockfall terrain).
creatures.visual_notes: Silky ash-gray fur with rust-colored spots, dark nose, and an extraordinarily thick ringed tail.

creatures.name: Pampas-Deer
creatures.education: Pampas deer have an extraordinary defense strategy: when a predator approaches, the stag flags his white tail and gallops away, leading the danger away while female deer and fawns drop flat into the grass to freeze like invisible stones.
creatures.exploration_trait: Decoy Sprint (Draws hostile monster attention away from fragile homestead structures).
creatures.visual_notes: Graceful reddish-tan deer with three-tined antlers, white eye rings, and bright white flashing tail.

creatures.name: Harpy-Sovereign
creatures.habitat: Ancient Emergent Rainforest Trees (over 200 ft tall)
creatures.education: Sovereign harpy eagles build massive nests in the crowns of giant kapok and Brazil nut trees that stand high above the rest of the forest. Pairs maintain the same nesting territory for decades, serving as the ultimate guardians of the rainforest canopy.
creatures.exploration_trait: Canopy Sovereign (Unlocks flight routes directly between emergent giant canopy observation towers).
creatures.visual_notes: Immense majestic eagle with slate-black wings, double feather crest, pure white torso, and five-inch curved talons.

creatures.name: Cappy-Patriarch
creatures.education: The elder patriarch of a wild capybara clan leads herds of up to 40 individuals with gentle wisdom. In indigenous stories, the giant grandfather capybara is honored as the peaceful diplomatic ambassador of all forest animals, bringing harmony wherever he rests.
creatures.exploration_trait: Sanctuary Harmony (Creates a zone of total harmony where wild animals do not flee or fight the player).
creatures.visual_notes: Colossal gentle grandfather capybara with rich chestnut fur, surrounded by resting birds and glowing mud-glow glyphs.
